scope: One live Chromium to production Next rewrite to FastAPI to OpenAI investigation

request.query: cart-service error rate spiked after the last deploy

report.summary: During the requested investigation window, cart-service had a threshold-validated 5xx error-rate anomaly, reaching 15.00pp from a near-zero baseline; the reported ratio is not meaningful. Sampled ERROR logs show repeated NullPointerException failures in PromotionEngine.applyDiscount at PromotionEngine.java:88, making a null-handling defect a plausible contributor. The findings do not establish that this was caused by the last deploy or that these exceptions account for all 5xx errors. No WARN logs or results from the separate PromotionEngine search were returned.

likely_causes.title: Null-handling defect in PromotionEngine.applyDiscount
likely_causes.rationale: Repeated NullPointerException errors at the same application method provide a plausible failure mechanism for cart-service errors, alongside the observed 5xx anomaly. The evidence does not prove these exceptions explain all 5xx responses or establish their timing relative to the metric change.

supporting_evidence.detail: 20 sampled cart-service ERROR occurrences report NullPointerException at com.shop.cart.PromotionEngine.applyDiscount(PromotionEngine.java:88); samples show version=v1.5.0 and timestamps from 2026-10-25T18:55:22+00:00 to 2026-10-25T19:14:22+00:00.
The threshold-validated cart-service 5xx metric shows an anomaly, emerging from a near-zero baseline and reaching 15.00pp; no ratio is meaningful.

next_steps: Verify deployment history, including whether v1.5.0 was the last deploy, and compare deploy timing with metric and exception trends.
Inspect PromotionEngine.applyDiscount at line 88 and correlate exception occurrences with failed requests and response status codes.
Retrieve request-rate and endpoint-level status-code data to quantify impact and check whether errors are concentrated in particular request types.
Confirm metric and log coverage throughout the requested interval; aggregate trends and sampled timestamps do not establish exact onset or continuous coverage.
